We explored ways to help him stay calmer and more focused, including desensitization, clicker training, pack walks, and enrichment activities like using a snuffle mat. Next Steps:Counter Condition & Desensitization on Walks: Start at a distance where Nasir notices other dogs but remains under threshold. Use a marker word (like "yes") or a clicker to reward him for looking at the dogs and staying composed. You can also scatter some treats on the grass/ground if it's safe to do so for Nasir to continue observing from the distance the other dog without reacting. Enrichment Course: Set up a backyard activity area using snuffle mats and different treats for Nasir to go sniff and explore, this will help exercise him without doing too much physical activity.Treat Value Testing: Experiment with different treats to identify high- and low-value rewards.Encouraging Check-Ins: Reward Nasir when he offers unprompted check-ins at home. Slowly start increasing the difficulty by moving to the backyard and practicing during walks. Prolong the connection by giving small rewards over the span of 5-10 second for the check-in. Practice Explicit Permission: Identify tricks Nasir can do and likes to do (like sit, down, spin). Identify things Nasir will work for (like meals, going outside on a walk, a toy). Ask nasir to perform a cue to access the real-life reward (going outside, food bowl). This will create a pattern of him checking in with you when he wants something and then you can give explicit permission. SummaryWe discussed how Nasir behaves on walks, his ability to settle in a crate, and his familiarity with basic cues. I suggested gradually desensitizing him to other dogs and being vigilant of his body language to identify moments where an emergency "u" turn would be appropriate. I agreed this could be a good strategy but suggested keeping enough distance at first and adjusting based on his body language. We also discussed the importance of strengthening their connection so DeQuency becomes more of a reference point for Nasir rather than relying solely on the leash.DeQuency, I hope this is helpful, please keep me updated!! HomeNotes: 4/1/2025 PARCEL – 2 Week Foster Questionnaire 3/23 General Personality I want to preface this note. Parcel ended up with some respiratory issues and was fixed so he has spent most of his time quarantined from out other pets. This has also meant that we have not gotten out to do a lot of things that we would have at this point. I would like to update this after he gets to fully integrate in a few weeks. Parcel is an even tempered happy go lucky guy. He is pretty chill most of the time and will go with the flow. He enjoys being around and playing with other dogs, fine being around cats, curious, wants to be friends, just not sure how. Most of all, he really craves human attention. He will jump and be a bit mouthy at times when he really wants attention, but we are working on this. He is incredibly gentile taking treats, not a food or treat aggressive, fully crate trained, does well on a leash and loves to go on walks, he enjoys being outside in the back yard, but does not want to be left out on his own, rides well in the car, likes all people and is happy to get attention.Daily Routine He goes outside to the bathroom first thing, then eats and out again before a short walk in the morning. I will let him out a few times during the day as he is not fully housebroken. Around dinner time he gets fed again and will go out to do his business immediately after he eats. He goes on a second longer walk in the afternoon/evening.What food do they eat? Dry dog food and treats.What would be an ideal home and family for your foster? A family with time to give him lots of attention. I think he really likes having a "big brother" and some cat siblings and would do fine in a house with other pets, but he would also be happy to get all of the attention. After he recovers, we will spend time out hiking some of the local parks and see what he thinks about that and his energy level. My current dog never stops.On a scale of 1 to 5 how housetrained are they? 3Does your foster use a kennel without excessive barking/whining, escape attempts, or destruction? Fully crate trained. He may whine very briefly when you walk away, but does not bark or act out. He will willingly go in the crate when asked.Where do they sleep at night? Currently he is sleeping in a seperate room/crate while he recovers from respiratory illness and his recent castration. However, I think he would be very happy to sleep with the rest of us.Do they sleep through the night? YesHas he / she been exposed to any kids? If yes, what ages? How did it go? We will introduce him to kids when he is fully recovered from his respiratory issues. He did meet 2 middle school kids on his first day at the house and was very happy to get attention and was very calm.Has he / she been exposed to any cats? If yes, how did it go? Yes, we have 3 cats and his initial engagements were very positive. Parcel was mildly curious, but did not chase or even become excited. Of course, this is the same dog that does not chase squirrels. I'm not sure he is really a dog! (just kidding).Do they prefer men or women? No preferenceDoes he / she live with another dog? Yes, I have a 67 lb mix. They were very happy to play. A day after their introduction, Parcel showed signs of respiratory illness which has meant that he has had to be quarantined, but they are both anxious to get to play soon.Has he / she been around other dogs? Parcel seems to like other dogs and is very respectful when meeting a new friend and then will be playful. We will set up many more doggie play dates in the neighborhood once he recovers from his respiratory issues.Does he / she know any basic commands? Which ones (Sit, stay, come, lay down, etc) ? Yes, he knows some commands: stay, sit (when you are in front of him), and come (but he may not always obey). We are working on some additional training.Is your foster dog leash reactive? What makes them bark/lunge on leash? Overall, Parcel walks well on the leash, he does not bark at anything so far on a leash and the only time he has lunged is when he gets a great big mouthful of leaves/grass or might get spooked by a loud car/truck. He walks fairly well on the leash, but has started to test his limits and will pull some. We are working on learning heal.What devices do you use to walk your dog? (Type of harness, collar, etc) from the shelter he came with an elizabethen collar and a harness with an end of a leash attached to both. He does better with this setup than the collar alone. Still experimenting hereLeash Walking Rating 4How does your foster do in the car? He rides pretty well in the car. While he will not jump into the car, he does not fight being picked up and put in the car. I think this has to do with his avoidance of jumping on furniture in the house rather than something specific to the car. He rides in the back seat in a hammock, but he does at times want to come up to the front seat. He seems to enjoy going for rides, but we have not been on many at this time.How does your foster do for a bath? its not his favorite activity, but he will let you bathe him without a fight and he loves get toweled off!Energy level 3How much exercise does it take to tire them out? This is hard to say as we have been keeping him sedentary due to the respiratory illness and getting fixed. But we go for walks of about a mile or so and he enjoys playing. But I do not see him keeping up on a 15 mile hike with my current dog.If they don't get enough exercise, what happens? He is not destructive at all.A perfect day for your foster would include ____________? Lots of human attention. He loves attention more than his doggie playmate. He would love a family that could spend a lot of one on one time.How cuddly are they? 4Favorite toys or games? He loves chew toys like rawhide but he also loves squeaky toys and will happily squeak and carry it around. He is not a ball or frisbee dog, he really couldn't care less about chasing a ball not matter how much my dog tries to get him to care about that fuzzy yellow thing.Tell us a fun story about your foster The first time that Parcel played with our dog Bode in the back yard, he would try to chase Bode but is not fast enough to keep up, so he learned to "hide" behind the retaining wall and jump out when Bode zoomed by and cut him off.I love my foster and think he/she is fabulous because _____________? He is just such a happy go lucky guy. Nothing really bothers him.What makes him/her nervous or unhappy? He wants attention and affection and will let you know that he is waiting impatiently.Overall, how are your foster's manners? (some examples: Jumps on people? Mouthy? Gets into trash?) When he really wants attention he can jump, but this seems to be reserved for people he knows -- I'll update as we meet more people. When we play he can get mouthy, but he is the most gentle mouthy dog I have ever seen!Does your foster have any behavioral issues or quirks? We are working on the basics right now, again with a little time and integration I will be able to provide more feedback here. One thing I will mention is that he does not jump on the furniture.
